text: Good morning everyone. Thank you all for being here. My name is Kyle, I'm a co founder of Multicoin Capital. This is Tarek, co founder and CEO at Kalshi, the largest prediction market in the U.S. tarek, can we start off you just tell us a little bit about your background?
speaker: A

text: Yeah, well thanks for having me. Very excited to be here. So we started the company out of MIT and you know, now people are talking about this sort of idea of prediction markets. But at the time kind of the notion of prediction markets was super niche corner of the Internet where we really came at sort of the idea from. I spent time at Goldman Sachs and Citadel. So really Tradfi and you know, the things that we were doing, the types of things that we were doing back in the day, we saw that a lot of institutional flow that was coming to us was actually asking us to give them some form of exposure to sort of whether Trump was going to win the 2016 election or lose it or Brexit was going to happen or not. So it's kind of very specific types of questions about the future. And what we were doing is we were using traditional assets, so like options, futures, equities to get them the exposure to the event they were looking for. But like that was super indirect. It was super expensive and obviously very inaccessible. Not everyone can go to Goldman Sachs and ask for an exotic product. So this was sort of the genesis of the idea. So there's a financial market for pricing stocks, credit, commodities, currencies, but there wasn't one for pricing just simple questions about the future that have economic and social relevance and realized that if we actually could build this, this sort of financial market could be one of the largest down the line because the one that the largest number of people could relate to and then number two, it could be one of the most useful because you're then pricing the future, you're making everybody smarter about what could happen for a variety of different things. There's going to be a hurricane in Florida. Who's going to win the election? You know, where is inflation going to be at the end of year? Is the Solana ETF going to get approved? And if you get smart about these questions, you can do all sorts of things like better decision making, better risk management and so on and so forth. So that was really how we started the company and went into this sort of long regulatory fight journey to get.

speaker: A

text: Yeah, I mean, I think, yeah. And I think you're right. Like, I think crypto and prediction markets are intertwined in many ways. I think. I think both are sort of new forms of financial systems. They also sort of have a lot of synergies. But one of the sort of ways they're very similar is they both had to fight for the right to exist. And, you know, I think crypto has done an incredible amount of progress in the last decade or so for prediction markets. There's a little bit of a difference. We were kind of alone in this sort of regulatory fight. So when we first started a company, we realized, like, this is illegal. Like, the US Government did not want these to be in the US and so we had to go through this sort of excruciatingly long journey. I mean, it was really three to three years and a half of convincing policymakers and the regulators to let us sort of do this in the US In a regulated and legal way. And, like, people ask a lot, like, what was the secret sauce? I mean, it really was sort of relentlessness. Like, if you do something for long enough, at some point you create enough of a movement momentum around you, then people start believing you. And then the more people start believing you, they become evangelists. And then over time, you know, and, like, you're seeing this with crypto right now, right? Like, you're. You know, you had Senator Haggerty on stage right now talking about, you know, that wasn't. That wasn't happening five years ago. Right. And so it's the same sort of thing happens. You have to create a wave and push it, push it so hard for so long that at some point the wave gets large enough that it can make a meaningful impact and start breaking down barriers. And so this is sort of. It was very simple. So this was really what happened in the Story of Kalshi for us, though, especially for the election market. And this was sort of the key moment that happened last year. We did have to sue the government. So we sued the government didn't let us do the election market for two to three years. We sued them over it. It was a very difficult decision because when you sue your own regulator, the federal government, they will hurt you in many ways. And that happened over the last few years. It was a very painful journey. But we believe we were right and we believe this should be legal at the end of the day. And we won, and it was totally worth it. So I would do it again in a heartbeat.

text: All right, next up, let's get into crypto. What exactly does Kalshi do with crypto today? Why are you here?

text: Yeah, so I mean look like any non traditionally crypto company. I think now that the regulatory environment sort of enables us to get into crypto. We've always in many ways like we always wanted to be in crypto, we just didn't have legal and regulated venues to do it. And you're seeing companies like us, companies like Robinhood, companies like a bunch of others like really leaning in very heavy in crypto and like oftentimes actually Solana is sort of one of the ecosystems of choice because it's trader friendly and and we're doing the same thing. So like I think now we're leading it very aggressively. Like I think the first is payment methods, payment rails, like if you're in tradfi and you've dealt with sort of traditional like payment infrastructure, it sucks. Fraud is very hard to manage. Conversion rates are bad and like you know, first, you know we launched stablecoins late last year. We launched like I think bitcoin early this year and this morning we launched Solana Deposits. So which we're super excited about. And over time I would say like one access to sort of wallets. I think there's large amounts of liquidity and money just sort of on chain. I think companies like ours want to sort of go to where the user is sitting and like basically access these wallets. Number Two, I think we're going to start over time posting transactions on the blockchain, you know, as a way to basically enable more transparent financial systems. Like in some ways right now we have on the database, we try to make it accessible on our website, but why not put it on chain and have anyone basically out there to see? And I think the third one is the thing that we were discussing a few months ago, like in this idea of modalities, which is over time, like if we basically build a layer on chain, we enable other builders to build on top of prediction markets. And we already see it in Tradfire. We would love to see it sort of in Defi, where people are basically building like weather apps that forecast the weather based on our weather forecast, or like apps that are sort of polling apps that like use our market forecast to forecast where, you know, who's going to win the next sort of primaries or who's going to take over Congress. And there's all these sort of. There's this entire, like, large application layer that can be built on top of prediction markets and the data that we have by a bunch of builders. And I can't think of a better ecosystem of builders than Solana or basically crypto more broadly. And so those are, I would say, the three sort of pillars that we're super excited about.
speaker: B

text: Is there any, you know, Kalshi has a DCM and a DCO license from the cftc. Is there any world in which y' all try and move some of that infrastructure on chain?
speaker: A

text: So maybe for context of crowd, like you know, since Dodd Frank, since the financial crisis, any financial instruments, financial derivative needs to be cleared by a regulated clearinghouse and clearing houses. What they do really fundamentally is they, you know, move money and then they kind of take care of like collateral management. So if you want to trade something that's worth $1,000, they decide how much you have to put up and then they manage that collateral. And right now that's done sort of a traditional banking infrastructure. And there's many reasons for it. But like, if you think about it from first principles, like over time there has to be some sort of on chain aspect to that. There has to be, like, there are things that like, you want, you know, the transparency is very important. I think, you know, the lack of reversibility is very important. And to me it's a question of, it's a matter of time. It's like a question of educating regulators and getting them comfortable with like, actually you can get most of the benefits that a Bank provides you without additional risk. And so why not? So I hope so. I hope the answer to that question is yes.

text: So I think two things. One is the space is now legal, right? Like, that's a very simple one. In the last election, there was this very key moment and that was, I think, both true for us, Kalshi and polymarket, our main competitor, where we were the only place where you can go and get truth about what was going to happen. So all the other polls were saying 50, 50, and like the only two places that were saying there was going to be a 62, 63% chance of Trump winning the election were calcium polymarket. And so that created in some ways a sort of like very sort of, you know, intense key moments where around a very key event, very, very critical, important event where people were like realizing, holy shit, these things are incredibly powerful, they're actually useful. And it kind of went mainstream. So one number that I left, like 500 million unique visitors came to our site on election night. So it's like 7% of the world population, I think something like that. That's a lot of people. And I think once you see the power of these markets, you realize like, oh, well, every time I have a question about the future, I'm gonna go to product prediction market.
